title: Number of 1 Bits
prompt:
Return the number of set bits (1s) in the binary representation of `n`. Treat `n` as a 32-bit value — negatives count their two's-complement bits.

**Example**: `11` (binary `1011`) → `3`; `-1` (all 32 bits set) → `32`.

Use the `n & (n - 1)` loop you drilled — it clears one set bit per iteration and handles negatives for free.
hints: Alternative: check each of 32 positions with `(n >> i) & 1`. Also fine, always 32 iterations.

solution.explanation: Brian Kernighan's trick: `n - 1` flips the lowest set bit and everything below it, so AND-ing erases exactly that bit. Loops once per set bit. The `!= 0` condition (not `> 0`) is what makes negative inputs terminate correctly.
